description: Start a new, empty part. Every part has the coordinate-system datum `origin`, whose planes a sketch is drawn on, as `add_sketch`'s `plane`: {"datum": "origin:xy"}, {"datum": "origin:yz"} or {"datum": "origin:zx"}.
name: new_part

description: Every operation a step can be: its kind (what `add_step` takes), label, group and what it does. Given a `kind`, that operation alone, with the arguments a new step starts with (`default_args`, the JSON `add_step` takes) and the form the editor shows for it (`form`: each field's key, control, label, value and, for a reference, the kinds of elements it accepts).

kind.description: The operation to describe in full, e.g. `extrude`.

name: list_operations

description: Add a step of the operation `kind` with `args` (its saved JSON, see `list_operations` with `kind`) at the end of the program, or before the step `before`. A step whose arguments do not read is refused and not added; one that reads but does not build is added, and its error says why. Answers with every step's status: an error names the step and what went wrong.

args.description: The step's arguments as saved in a .geop file.

before.description: The step to add it before; the end of the program if left out.

id.description: The step's id (letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `.`); chosen from the operation's label if left out. Later steps refer to what this one builds by it, e.g. `extrude(<id>)`.

name: add_step

description: Change the step `id`: the keys of `args` replace those of its arguments (the others stay), so one dimension can be changed alone. The program is rebuilt from that step on.
name: edit_step

description: Remove the step `id`. Steps that referred to what it built then fail, and say so.
name: delete_step

description: Run the whole program and report every step: its summary, whether it ran, and its error with the kernel's context if it failed; and the solids the part has.
name: run

description: The names of the part's elements as they are now, for typed references: solids, faces (with their solid), edges (with their faces), vertices, sketches, datums and what else the part lists (threads, placed parts). A face is referred to by its name, as a sketch's plane {"face": ...}; an edge by its name, as in a fillet's `edges`.
name: list_elements

description: Ask about the part: `mass_properties` (volume, area and centroid of every solid; its mass and inertia if its part has a material, null if not), `interference` (which solids overlap), or `measure` with `elements` (a point, a length, an area, a radius; the distance and angle between two).

elements.description: For `measure`: one or two elements, each {"kind": "vertex"|"edge"|"face"|"datum", "name": ...}.

name: inspect
